def: Managed service for provisioning, managing, and deploying TLS/SSL certificates for AWS services and connected resources.
Layer-7 load balancer that routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic based on request content (path, host, headers, query strings).
A pre-configured virtual machine template that defines the OS, software, and configuration for launching EC2 instances.
A globally unique identifier for every AWS resource, formatted as arn:partition:service:region:account-id:resource.
Automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances in a group based on demand, health checks, or schedules.
An isolated data centre (or cluster of DCs) within an AWS Region. Multiple AZs in a Region provide high availability.
An open-source IaC framework that lets you define cloud infrastructure using TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, or Go.
AWS's native IaC service. You declare resources in JSON/YAML templates; CloudFormation provisions them as a "stack".
Records API calls and account activity across AWS as event logs — the audit trail for compliance and forensics.
Observability service for metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards, and anomaly detection across AWS services.
Fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.
Persistent block storage volumes attached to EC2 instances — like a virtual hard drive.
Virtual servers (instances) in the cloud. You choose instance type, OS (AMI), and networking. The core compute primitive.
Fully managed container image registry for storing, managing, and deploying Docker and OCI images.
AWS's container orchestration service. Run containers on EC2 or serverless via Fargate — no Kubernetes required.
Managed Kubernetes control plane. AWS handles the master nodes; you manage worker nodes or use Fargate.
Distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets (EC2, ECS tasks, Lambda). Three types: ALB, NLB, GLB.
Serverless compute engine for ECS and EKS. Run containers without managing the underlying EC2 instances.
Threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity using ML, anomaly detection, and threat intelligence.
Controls who (identity) can do what (actions) on which resources (ARNs). Foundation of all AWS security.
Creates and manages cryptographic keys for encrypting data at rest and in transit across AWS services.
Run code without provisioning servers. You upload a function, Lambda executes it on triggers, you pay per invocation and duration.
Layer-4 load balancer for ultra-high performance, static IP requirements, and TCP/UDP/TLS traffic.
Managed relational databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MariaDB, and Aurora.
Highly available DNS service with health checking, traffic routing policies, and domain registration.
Object storage with 11 9s of durability. Store virtually unlimited objects; used for backups, static assets, data lakes, and more.
AWS Organizations policy type that restricts what IAM permissions can be granted across entire OUs or accounts.
AWS SDKs provide language-specific APIs (boto3 for Python, aws-sdk for JS/TS, etc.) to interact with AWS programmatically.
Managed pub/sub messaging. Publishes messages to topics; subscribers receive via HTTP, SQS, Lambda, email, SMS.
Fully managed message queuing. Decouples producers and consumers; supports standard and FIFO queues.
Operational management hub: Parameter Store for config/secrets, Session Manager for shell access without SSH, Patch Manager.
Open-source IaC tool using HCL. Manages multi-cloud resources declaratively via providers. Widely used alongside or instead of CDK/CFN.
Logically isolated network in AWS. You control IP ranges (CIDR), subnets, route tables, internet gateways, and security groups.
Protects web apps from common exploits (SQLi, XSS, OWASP Top 10) at the ALB, CloudFront, or API Gateway edge.
Distributed tracing service. Traces requests through microservices to identify latency bottlenecks and errors.
